issues.title: [Sprint 3] Add automated AI review and bundle audit to pull requests
issues.body:
Owner: Anthony Saltat
Estimate: 1 working day
Dependencies: #12

Context
Mentor requirement: use an AI agent to check the repository automatically (like CodeRabbit) and use REA to reverse-engineer and verify what we ship.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CodeRabbit is configured with TSEK's project rules and reviews every pull request, including stacked ones.
- [ ] A TSEK AI review workflow posts one structured, validated review comment per pull request and never blocks work when the AI provider fails.
- [ ] Secrets in a diff are redacted before the diff is sent to the AI provider.
- [ ] A frontend bundle audit fails the pipeline when the built frontend contains secrets or calls OpenAI or the database directly.
- [ ] The REA audit procedure is documented, and the first audit result is recorded.

Completion evidence
- [ ] Link the implementation branch and reviewed pull request.
- [ ] Attach passing checks and an example AI review comment.

pulls.title: ci: add AI pull request review, bundle audit, and REA audit guide
pulls.body:
Closes #46

## What changed
- **CodeRabbit** (`.coderabbit.yaml`): TSEK-specific review rules for the frontend, backend, migrations, tests, and workflows. Reviews every pull request, including stacked ones like #5 and #45, which it skipped before.
- **TSEK AI review** (`ai-review.yml` + `.github/scripts/ai-review.mjs`): on every pull request, sends the diff to `gpt-4.1-mini`, validates the structured review against a JSON schema, and posts one comment that updates on each push.
  - Automatic checks flag possible secrets and frontend code that calls OpenAI or the database.
  - Secrets are redacted before the diff is sent to OpenAI.
  - Advisory only: provider errors, timeouts, and invalid output are reported in the comment and never block the pull request.
- **Frontend bundle audit** (`bundle-audit.yml`): builds the frontend and fails if `dist` contains an API key, the OpenAI endpoint, a database connection string, a Neon host, or a server secret name. It prints file names only, so a leaked key never reaches the public log.
- **`docs/AI_REPO_CHECKS.md`**: how each check works, setup, and the REA audit procedure.

## How it was tested
- AI review script, against fake OpenAI and GitHub servers: valid review (comment created), second push (same comment updated), invalid AI output, HTTP 500 with one retry, and missing API key. All five post a clear comment and exit successfully. A planted OpenAI key and database password were redacted before the request to OpenAI.
- Bundle audit on real builds of `main` and PR #3: no false alarms. With a planted key and OpenAI call in `dist`: fails and prints only the file name.
- YAML for all files parsed; script syntax checked.

## Setup needed after merge
- Create an OpenAI project `tsek-ci` with a low budget and add its key as the repository secret `AI_REVIEW_OPENAI_API_KEY`. Until then, the comment shows the automatic checks and says the AI review was skipped.
- Run the first REA audit and record it in `docs/AI_REPO_CHECKS.md`.

pulls.title: ci: add staging environment and deploy it before production
pulls.body:
Closes #24

## What changed
- Every merge to `main` now deploys to **staging** first, smoke-tests it, and only then deploys **production**. A failed staging release never reaches production.
- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys either environment, using the same secret and variable names in the `staging` and `production` GitHub environments.
- The smoke test waits up to about 9 minutes for Render to wake and rebuild. If `/health` reports a `commit`, it waits for this run's commit, so it tests the new release instead of the old one.
- Runs on `main` are no longer cancelled midway by a newer push; superseded PR runs still are.
- `frontend/vercel.json` turns off Vercel's automatic deploys from `main`, so production goes live only through the pipeline after staging passes. PR previews still run.
- `docs/STAGING.md` explains the setup for Neon, Render, Vercel, OpenAI, and GitHub.

## Already configured in repository settings
- Created the `staging` GitHub environment.
- Both `staging` and `production` accept deployments from protected branches only (`main`).

## How it was tested
- Workflow YAML parsed and job wiring checked (`checks → staging → production`).
- The smoke-test script was run against a local fake backend: no commit field (pass), matching commit (pass), older commit (fails after retries), backend down (fails after retries).
- Until the hosting secrets and URLs are added, deploy and smoke-test steps are skipped and listed in the run summary, as before.

## Still needed (hosting accounts)
- Neon `staging` branch, Render `tsek-api-staging` service, Vercel `tsek-staging` project, separate staging OpenAI key.
- Add each environment's deploy hooks and URLs in **Settings → Environments**.

pulls.title: ci: require every pull request to close an issue
pulls.body:
Closes #6

## What changed
- Add a `PR links an issue` check. It fails any pull request into `main` whose description has no `Closes #N` (or `Fixes` / `Resolves`).
- Add a pull request template that starts with `Closes #`.
- Add `CONTRIBUTING.md` documenting 1 issue = 1 branch = 1 pull request, pulling `main` before starting work, teammate review, and the rules enforced on `main`.

## Why
Course rule: every issue is delivered through its own reviewed pull request. Before this change, none of the open or merged pull requests referenced an issue.

## How it was tested
- The issue-link pattern was tested with 9 sample descriptions. A closing keyword followed by an issue number passes, with or without a colon, and for several issues at once. A keyword with no number, a keyword inside another word, plain text, and an empty description fail.
- This pull request must pass the new check itself.

## After merge (DevOps)
